tools.name: log_anything
tools.description: Log food, drinks, water, exercise, or a weigh-in from one natural-language sentence — the same parser as the app's voice logging. Examples: 'two eggs and toast', '30 minute run', '3 glasses of water', 'weighed 184 this morning'. Spoken dates like 'yesterday I had pizza' work. Describe the FOOD, not

tools.name: log_exercise
tools.description: Log structured exercise with a known calorie burn. For an ESTIMATED burn from plain text, use log_anything ('30 minute run').

tools.name: log_weight
tools.description: Log a weigh-in in pounds. The newest reading also becomes the user's current weight (drives their calorie targets).

tools.name: log_water
tools.description: Log water — glasses (8 fl oz each) or an exact amount_fl_oz. Defaults to 1 glass.

tools.name: get_today
tools.description: Today's complete picture: calorie/macro totals vs targets, water, streak, exercises, and the item-by-item food log (`recent`: every logged item's name, calories, macros, ingredients). Each `recent` item's `id` works with update_log to correct mistakes.

tools.name: get_day
tools.description: Everything logged on a specific day, INCLUDING each food item's name and nutrition (same shape as get_today). Use this to answer “what did I eat yesterday / on <date>”. Each `recent` item's `id` works with update_log to correct mistakes.

tools.name: get_progress
tools.description: Daily calorie/macro/exercise TOTALS over time + the weight trend (no food item names — use get_day for what was actually eaten).

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Who the user is: name/handle/email, health profile, calorie/macro targets, and derived metrics.

tools.name: update_log
tools.description: Correct an existing FOOD log: title, nutrition numbers, the ingredient list, meal, or time-of-day. Read get_today/get_day first — each item in `recent` (type "food") carries the `id` to pass here. Send ONLY the fields to change; values are absolute for the item as logged. findings.detail: Description of "update_log" is 1074 chars, far longer than this server's median (128). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_me · Private data: update_log · Public sink: get_me, update_log · Destructive: log_anything, log_exercise.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_me · Private data: update_log · Public sink: get_me, update_log · Destructive: log_anything, log_exercise

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
